topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture series, student cohorts, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer arises from genetic and epigenetic disruptions to normal differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture, alongside experimental models used to study these processes.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and the transition from benign to malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained, benign growths to invasive and metastatic malignancies across clinical, histological, and anatomical contexts.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions for naming benign and malignant neoplasms across tissue types.

topics.label: Pathophysiology of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the physiological and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative epidemiology and evolutionary incidence of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the prevalence of different tumor types in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, histological foundations, and clinical efficacy of early detection and screening programmes across different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This closing framing concludes the lecture with a review of learning outcomes and reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
